verdict.summary: Any ClickUp Workspace owner or admin can create an OAuth app in Settings > Apps, and any ClickUp user can then authorize it with no review, no scopes and no listing step. The trade-offs are coarse access (no scopes, so the token can act on everything the user can see in the authorized Workspaces) and a 100 requests/min per-token limit on most plans.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Create the app with a name and redirect URL, copy client_id and secret, run the authorization-code flow. Nothing is reviewed.

timeToProd.assumes: A standard OAuth app that reads and writes tasks for any ClickUp user who authorizes their Workspaces; there is no slower path to choose.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: ClickUp's docs describe no review, approval or install cap for OAuth apps. Absence of a review step is our reading of the docs, not an explicit statement.

prerequisites.item: Owner or admin role in a ClickUp Workspace (a free Workspace you create works)
prerequisites.why: 'Only Workspace owners or admins can create OAuth apps.'
The redirect URL is set when creating the app. ClickUp warns that 'Non-SSL redirect URIs may not be supported in the future.'

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Non-SSL URIs apparently work today, but we didn't test it.

prerequisites.item: A server to hold the client secret
prerequisites.why: The token exchange sends client_id, client_secret and code to the token endpoint.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: We saw no PKCE support documented.

scopeTiers.tier: Workspace authorization (ClickUp has no OAuth scopes)
scopeTiers.impact: The user chooses which Workspaces to authorize, and the token works across them with that user's permissions. You can't ask for read-only access, so your privacy policy should explain why the agent needs full access.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The official page doesn't mention scopes. Nango states outright that ClickUp doesn't use scopes.

scopeTiers.tier: Personal API token (single user, not for distribution)
scopeTiers.impact: Fine for prototyping against your own Workspace. ClickUp says apps used by other people should use the OAuth flow.

steps.title: Sign in as a Workspace owner or admin
steps.detail: Use an existing Workspace where you're owner/admin, or create a free Workspace for development.

steps.title: Create the OAuth app
steps.detail: Avatar (top right) > Settings > Apps > Create new app. Enter a name and redirect URL, then copy the client_id and secret.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The menu path may differ slightly by ClickUp version.

steps.title: Implement the authorize redirect
steps.detail: Send users to https://app.clickup.com/api?client_id={client_id}&redirect_uri={redirect_uri}&state={state}. No scope parameter is needed.

steps.title: Exchange the code for a token
steps.detail: POST client_id, client_secret and code to https://api.clickup.com/api/v2/oauth/token. Store the access token encrypted; send it as Authorization: Bearer.

steps.title: Discover authorized Workspaces
steps.detail: Call Get Authorized Teams (Workspaces) after connecting to learn which Workspaces the user granted, and route later calls by team ID.

steps.title: Add rate-limit handling
steps.detail: Read X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-RateLimit-Reset, back off on HTTP 429, and size background sync to the 100 requests/min limit that applies to most plans.

steps.title: Test with a second account
steps.detail: Authorize the app from a different ClickUp user and Workspace to confirm the flow works outside your own Workspace.

steps.title: Launch
steps.detail: Put the Connect ClickUp button live. No submission or approval step is documented.

blockers.symptom: No 'Create new app' button in Settings > Apps
blockers.cause: Only Workspace owners or admins can create OAuth apps.
blockers.fix: Create your own free Workspace, or ask an owner/admin to create the app.
Re-copy the credentials from Settings > Apps.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: Observed by POSTing dummy credentials to https://api.clickup.com/api/v2/oauth/token on 2026-10-20.

blockers.cause: The request has no Authorization header.
blockers.fix: Send Authorization: Bearer {access_token} for OAuth tokens.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: Observed on GET https://api.clickup.com/api/v2/user without a token on 2026-10-20.

blockers.symptom: HTTP 429 after about 100 calls in a minute
blockers.cause: Free Forever, Unlimited and Business Workspaces allow 100 requests per minute per token.
blockers.fix: Wait until X-RateLimit-Reset, batch work, and prefer webhooks over polling.

blockers.symptom: Agent can't see data in a Workspace the user belongs to
blockers.cause: The user didn't authorize that Workspace during consent.
blockers.fix: Send the user back to the authorization URL to add Workspaces.

nuances.text: 'The access token currently does not expire. This is subject to change.' There is no documented refresh token, so plan for re-authorization if ClickUp adds expiry.
Rate limits are per token and depend on the plan of the Workspace hosting the token: 100/min on Free Forever, Unlimited and Business; 1,000 on Business Plus; 10,000 on Enterprise.
No scopes means the token can do anything the user can do in the authorized Workspaces. Security-conscious customers may push back, and your agent should enforce its own read/write limits.
ClickUp doesn't publish an OIDC discovery document, so 'Sign in with ClickUp' means calling the user endpoint with the access token.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: https://app.clickup.com/.well-known/openid-configuration returned the web app's HTML shell, and api.clickup.com returned 'something went wrong', on 2026-10-20.

nuances.text: The core API is v2, with some newer surfaces (Docs, Chat) on v3 paths. OAuth tokens work for both.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: From a third-party API report card. We didn't confirm in official docs.
